portion_doctrine: Segments 21-30 are tutorial transcripts covering deployment, automation, and AI-assisted development. Core operating methods center on three deployment patterns (loops, scheduled tasks, modal/trigger.dev), Claude Code workflow methodology (explore-plan-code-commit), dynamic workflows for large-scale document processing, and SaaS framework integration with payment systems. Most content is instructional walkthrough rather than actionable doctrine. Gold: deployment trade-offs, multicontext plan persistence via GitHub issues, Stripe MCP integration patterns.
operating_rules: Loop scheduling: /loop for recurring tasks (max 7 days desktop, terminal gets more features)
Desktop vs cloud routines: local needs machine on, cloud routines run 24/7 on Anthropic infrastructure (15 runs/day max plan)
Cloud routines: 1 hour minimum interval, can be triggered via API/GitHub webhooks
Cron jitter: tasks fire up to 30 minutes after scheduled time to avoid API throttling
Explore-plan-code-commit workflow: shift+tab to enter plan mode before code
Plan mode: Claude reads only, no file edits - use for codebase research before implementation
Multi-phase plan persistence: save plans as GitHub issues to preserve context across sessions
Context management: check context window regularly, use /clear between unrelated tasks
Modal vs Trigger.dev: Modal is Python serverless (more script-like), Trigger.dev uses TypeScript (more agentic)
Managed Agents: Anthropic's official service but offers less flexibility than self-hosted routines
Hooks: event-driven automations (post-tool use, pre-tool use, session start/end) for layered workflows
Dynamic workflows trigger: include 'build a workflow' in prompt to invoke agent teams
Workflow vs single agent: use workflows for tasks requiring 5+ agents, comprehensive audits, large-scale document processing
Workflow batching: agents queue, don't all spawn at once - completion triggers next batch
Devil's advocate pattern: secondary agents in workflows refute and double-check primary insights
Stripe MCP: no API keys needed, use built-in connector from profile settings
Stripe connector permissions: grant read/write access, then use MCP queries instead of manual API calls
Superbase integration: MCP handles table creation, data insertion, schema updates via natural language
Playwright MCP: automated browser testing, visual verification of UI changes during builds
Sandbox mode: test Stripe products/prices in test environment before moving to live
Recurring prices: use Stripe API directly if MCP lacks that capability (edge case)
Database vs constants: database stores dynamic user subscription state, constants store static plan definitions
Hosted Stripe checkout: preferred over custom checkout for simplicity (Stripe handles sensitive data)
Plan mode before implementation: always review Claude's multi-phase plan before execution
Sub-agent code review: run before commit to catch errors before pushing
prompts: Set up a loop every 10 minutes to [task name]
Set up a loop to do [task] and automatically kill it after 24 hours
Build a workflow that reads every [data source] in parallel and flags [specific issues]
Build a workflow that audits every file under [path] for [security concern], has a second agent refute each finding, return only confirmed issues
Generate images for a YouTube script (one image per timestamp) using Higgsfield skill
I want you to run the following command: [Stripe/Superbase MCP command]
Evaluate the tech stack of this app and give me recommendations on where to deploy
Do a dedicated pass on the mobile version: think about what should be hidden, tightened, resized
Find the bugs: [brief error description] and expected result vs actual result
Check your context window usage and report
gates: Session expiry: desktop loops max 7 days, terminal loops theoretically longer but jitter applies
Cloud routine cap: 5 runs/day on Pro, 15 on Max, 25 on Team/Enterprise
Minimum interval: cloud routines cannot run more frequently than 1 hour
Workflow cost: watch token usage - 3 million tokens for 51-agent comprehensive audit is normal but expensive
Sandbox requirement: always test Stripe in sandbox before moving to live
MCP limitations: some capabilities (e.g., recurring prices) may require direct API fallback
Plan review: always review multi-phase plans before approval to catch unnecessary complexity
Context rotation: clear context and save via GitHub issues when crossing 70% utilization
content_ideas: Comparison: loops vs scheduled tasks vs modal vs trigger.dev (decision matrix)
Multi-context workflow pattern: GitHub issue persistence deep-dive
Stripe + Superbase + Claude Code full SaaS integration walkthrough
Dynamic workflow token economics: when the cost is worth it
Hooks as automation glue: layering multiple event-driven rules
Plan mode discipline: how to avoid scope creep in multi-phase builds
contradictions: Desktop loops end after 3 days in desktop app but 7 days in terminal (documented behavior difference)
Managed Agents promised but reviewer notes they lack flexibility vs self-hosted (design tension)
Claude can refuse React components for static sites but may suggest complex setups anyway (implementation discipline)
weird_gold: Cron jitter is undocumented API-protection pattern: tasks fire up to 30 minutes late by design
Terminal loop clearing behavior: /clear in terminal doesn't kill crons (different from desktop)
Playwright MCP used during dev, but builder disables it mid-build to avoid quality-check overhead (edge case)
GitHub issue workflow: treating issues as plan persistence layer (meta-automation pattern)
Stripe sandbox mode required before live: mental model shift from 'test then deploy' to 'scaffold test scaffold live'
Devil's advocate agent pattern in dynamic workflows: agents not just parallel-executing, they're explicitly refuting each other
Stripe constants file + database pattern: static plan config separate from dynamic user subscription state (architectural principle)
